top_story.headline: ICE seeks a no-bid temporary detention structure for 100 detainees in Batavia, New York
top_story.dek: The agency cites a loss of state and local detention space; the sole-source value is redacted.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to modify its existing detention services contract with Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC to add a temporary structure for up to 100 detainees, with medical infrastructure and armed guards, at the Batavia Service Processing Center. It says it has an increased need for detention beds in New York because of changes affecting state and local detention space and cooperation.

The agency says only the incumbent can do the work without duplicated cost and security risk, and calls the structure a temporary measure while longer-term capacity in the Buffalo area is arranged. The value is redacted in the public document.
Separately, the General Services Administration is raising the ceiling on an Army intelligence support task order held by CACI by $152,779,419 without new competition.

sections.headline: ICE seeks a no-bid temporary detention structure for 100 detainees at Batavia, New York
paragraphs: 57 new sole-source justifications and 1,000 new solicitations; 84 amendments or reposts of notices already covered in earlier editions are not repeated. Five justifications stand out, four tied to immigration enforcement or the Department of Homeland Security, and one is a $152.8 million ceiling increase for Army intelligence support.

blocks.title: ICE gets a no-bid temporary detention structure for 100 detainees at its Batavia, New York facility
meta: Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC
value redacted
only one company can do it
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (Department of Homeland Security)
blocks.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to modify its existing detention services contract with Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC of Herndon, Virginia to add a temporary structure holding up to 100 detainees of all security levels, plus medical and environmental infrastructure and armed guard services, at the Batavia Service Processing Center. The agency says it has "an increased need for detention beds in New York due to changes affecting the availability of state and local detention space and cooperation with local detention facilities," and that using another vendor would duplicate cost and add operational and security risk. The justification describes the structure as a temporary solution while longer-term capacity for the Buffalo area is arranged; the dollar value is redacted.

blocks.title: Army intelligence support task order gets a $152.8 million ceiling increase without new competition
meta: CACI
$152,779,419 ceiling increase
skipped the competition among existing contract holders
General Services Administration, for the U.S. Army C5ISR Center
blocks.text: The General Services Administration is raising the ceiling on the Global Operational Support, Information Insight, and Threat task order, awarded to CACI on May 20, 2024 with a ceiling of $414,857,176, for the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command C5ISR Center. The justification calls it a logical follow-on and says demand for intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and counter-drone support exceeded estimates, citing the war in Ukraine, tensions involving Iran and drone incursions in the northeastern United States. It also says internal funding realignments "have been completely exhausted," leaving a ceiling increase as the only way to sustain operations.

blocks.title: ICE reserves 366 parking spaces near its Washington headquarters from a single garage, citing the return-to-office order
meta: Potomac Center CF, LLC
value redacted
only one company can do it
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (Department of Homeland Security)
blocks.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is the lead tenant of Potomac Center South at 550 12th Street SW in Washington, D.C., and wants 366 indoor spaces in its underground garage for government-owned vehicles from Potomac Center CF, LLC. The justification cites the executive order on returning to in-person work and says the garage offers emergency access and egress to ICE headquarters during protests and building lockdowns. For market research, officials phoned four nearby facilities; two SP+ locations could have accommodated the need but were under construction. The request went to one vendor by informal quote, and the value is redacted.

blocks.title: TSA's sole-source help desk award is cut back after a protest, and the agency will now compete it
meta: Quasars
value redacted
only one company can do it
Transportation Security Administration (Department of Homeland Security)
blocks.text: The Transportation Security Administration awarded Quasars, the incumbent, a five-year sole-source task order on August 20, 2026 for the Online Learning Center help desk, which serves about 70,000 users. After an agency-level protest, the justification says the agency "has taken corrective action to conduct a competitive procurement," and this modification shortens performance to no later than May 19, 2027 to keep services running meanwhile. This is an award made before competition that the agency is now partly unwinding.

blocks.title: Court-ordered family reunification services go to the International Organization for Migration again because the government ran out of time to compete them
meta: International Organization for Migration
no value given
urgent need, no time to compete
U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (Department of Homeland Security)
blocks.text: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is giving the International Organization for Migration a follow-on contract for support services tied to the Miss L. v. Immigration and Customs Enforcement settlement, under which families separated at the border are reunified in the United States. The incumbent contract began August 13, 2021 and ran through September 12, 2026 after option periods. The justification says the Secretary of Homeland Security decided in late fiscal year 2025 to move administration of the services to the agency, and that the timing of later decisions left too little time for a competitive procurement.

items: Department of the Army — armed guard security in Erbil, Iraq for Combined Joint Task Force–Operation Inherent Resolve; GardaWorld Federal Services; value not given, urgent need with about 20 days to mobilize. The Army issued a notice to proceed on September 10, 2026 and awarded the order as an undefinitized contract action before the justification was posted (W519TC26FA649JEFO).

Washington Headquarters Services — two-month bridge contract, plus four one-month options through April 5, 2027, for project management and consulting support to the Department of Defense ManTech program; PM2 Strategies; value redacted. The prior task order was already extended six months through October 5, 2026 (HQ003426PE158).

National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — network operations modernization and integration services for the Department of Commerce; ANG Signal, the incumbent; $8,226,672 over up to two years (REQUIREMENTS-26-1617).
National Aeronautics and Space Administration — orbital safety analysis for satellite conjunction assessment and collision avoidance; Omitron, Inc.; $47,453,711 (80GSFC26D0010JOFOC).

Department of Homeland Security (Office of Procurement Operations) — fingerprint matching software, hardware, maintenance and 24-hour support for its biometric systems; THALES DIS USA Inc., which the justification says holds proprietary interfaces no other vendor can access; value redacted (SSJ_FY26_0190).

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — Hootsuite social media management platform and Talkwalker visual recognition for its public affairs office; Hootsuite Inc.; brand-name only; value redacted (JA-26-0292).
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — interim contract for operations and maintenance of the Visa Security Program Tracking System software; Steampunk Inc.; value redacted (70CTD026FR0000055).

Department of the Navy — extension of financial management data transformation services including Navy budget orchestration; KPMG; skipped competition among existing contract holders; value redacted (N0018926FZ108).
U.S. Customs and Border Protection — six-month extension of process development support for its Office of Facilities and Asset Management; Constant Solutions, LLC; $1,173,086 (20157583).

sections.headline: No new contract awards of $100,000 or more to report
paragraphs: No new-to-report awards over $2 million and no new awards between $100,000 and $2 million appeared in the USAspending sweep for September 13 through October 8, 2026.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files approved in this window
paragraphs: No new apportionment documents or spend plan changes were flagged by the Office of Management and Budget between October 3 and October 8, 2026. The routine monitoring of federal apportionment activity found no items requiring editorial attention or highlighting.

footer.coverage_window: October 3-8, 2026 (Pacific time) for SAM.gov and OMB; a trailing sweep from September 13 for USAspending contract actions.
